item.title: [136] Even Trump’s own supporters suspect latest 'assassination attempt' was staged
item.description:
President Donald Trump was seemingly the target of an assassination attempt on Saturday — yet millions of Americans believe the event was “staged.”

“Trump’s focus on his planned redecoration in the face of an apparent attempt on his life – the third in less than two years — has provoked a barrage of conspiracy theories,” wrote The Telegraph's Ed Cumming on Monday. Mere hours after Cole Thomas Allen allegedly tried to storm the White House Correspondents Dinner to shoot Trump, Trump called a press conference to demand completed construction of his proposed $400 million White House ballroom, Cumming pointed out, fueling the conspiracies.

“The most prominent is that Trump and his administration staged the attack to help shore up the ballroom project, which he hopes to have completed before he leaves office in early 2029,” Cumming reported. “Authorities have stated they believe Allen acted alone and left a ‘manifesto’ in which he clearly stated he wanted to target officials in the Trump administration. But according to a report by The New York Times, the term ‘staged’ appeared in more than 300,000 posts on Twitter by noon on Sunday.”

He added, “On Bluesky, the social media network with a more Left-wing user base, many posts simply stated ‘staged’. Several prominent accounts reshared theories — without evidence — that were skeptical of the official version of events.”

The skepticism is not limited to liberals. As Cumming pointed out, the flurry of supposed assassination attempts on Trump — as well as his habit of politically exploiting them to vilify his critics and push his agenda — has raised suspicions everywhere.

item.title: [ 64] Life of an ICC judge under Trump sanctions: no bank, no email, nothing
item.description:
https://www.thetimes.com/us/news-today/article/international-criminal-court-judges-sanctioned-by-trump-9jj0qktzr
They cannot book Ubers, Deliveroo or order from Amazon. They cannot access family photos saved on iCloud nor use Microsoft Word. Their credit cards and bank accounts have been cancelled. They cannot charge electric cars, read a Kindle or watch Netflix, nor book an Airbnb.
They are not terrorists or narco-traffickers but eminent judges and prosecutors at the International Criminal Court (ICC), as well as a special rapporteur on human rights for the United Nations.

Their daily lives have been made a nightmare having been put under US sanctions by President Trump, joining a list of al-Qaeda and Isis members, mafia bosses and Iran’s most hardline clerics and Revolutionary Guards — only in their case it is for trying to bring international justice.

“They have made us financial and technological outcasts,” said Francesca Albanese, 49, an Italian legal scholar who has been UN special rapporteur on human rights in Palestinian territories since 2022. “Our credit cards and bank accounts are cancelled. We cannot make payments. We cannot receive payments.”

Albanese was sanctioned last July after she issued a report in Geneva accusing a number of major corporations of being complicit in what she called Israel’s “genocidal campaign” in Gaza. Among them were 20 American companies including the arms producers Lockheed Martin and Palantir.
Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, responded by imposing sanctions, calling Albanese “unfit” for her role and accusing her of “unabashed antisemitism” and “biased and malicious activities against the US and its ally Israel”.

The 1,052-word missive obtained by The Post Sunday morning — signed Cole ‘coldForce’ ‘Friendly Federal Assassin’ Allen” — outlined his “rules of engagement” for the shooting and stated he believed it was his righteous duty to target administration officials.

Cole Allen’s manifesto in full:

> I apologize to all of the people I traveled next to, all the workers who handled my luggage, and all the other non-targeted people at the hotel who I put in danger simply by being near.

> I apologize to everyone who was abused and/or murdered before this, to all those who suffered before I was able to attempt this, to all who may still suffer after, regardless of my success or failure.

> I don’t expect forgiveness, but if I could have seen any other way to get this close, I would have taken it. Again, my sincere apologies.

item.title: [ 94] /pkp/ - Pokopia General #20
item.description:
Sleepless Knight Edition

>F.A.Q

Complete list of Pokémon here
https://www.serebii.net/pokemonpokopia/availablepokemon.shtml

>Can I have more than one world in the same console?
Yes. You can have different saves for each profile. It's not like AC.

>What about cloud saves?
Yes. Unlike every other Pokémon game, this one does support cloud saves.

>Does it feature a real time clock? Can I change the console's date to progress faster?
Yes. There's no downside to moving forward or backward.

>Is my favorite Pokemon in?
List is still being updated https://www.serebii.net/pokemonpokopia/availablepokemon.shtml

>I didn't like ACNH, will I like this one?
Similarities with ACNH end at the UI; game is a lot faster, with more activities and a proper ~40h long story mode. If you've played DQ Builders 2, you know what you're getting into.

>Combat? Breakable tools?
No combat, no breakable tools. There's a stamina system in place, but it's very easy to manage.

>Should I start building a mega project or finish the story?
FINISH THE STORY! Or, at the very least, complete Beach and Ridges.

>6DXL PD6F
Island made by a random Japanese person with one of every item and habitat. NOT a dev island.

item.title: [ 42] Trump fires the entire National Science Board
item.description:
Federal funding for scientific research was already in turmoil.
https://www.theverge.com/science/918769/trump-fires-the-entire-national-science-board

Multiple sources are reporting that the Trump administration has dismissed the entire National Science Board (NSB). The NSB advises the president and Congress on the National Science Foundation (NSF), which has already been funding research at historically low levels and has seen significant delays in doling out that funding. The NSF has been fundamental in helping develop technology used in MRIs, cellphones, and it even helped get Duolingo get off the ground.

In a statement, Zoe Lofgren, the ranking Democrat on the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee, said:
>“This is the latest stupid move made by a president who continues to harm science and American innovation. The NSB is apolitical. It advises the president on the future of NSF. It unfortunately is no surprise a president who has attacked NSF from day one would seek to destroy the board that helps guide the Foundation. Will the president fill the NSB with MAGA loyalists who won’t stand up to him as he hands over our leadership in science to our adversaries? A real bozo the clown move.”
